reflection_diagnosis.causal_diagnosis: The policy under iter_001 achieves 20% success-like terminal rate but 80% timeout. The dominant component by absolute return is fuel_penalty (-52.66), which is 4.22x the next component and 65x the positive objective budget. The shaping_reward (progress-delta) provides weak positive signal (mean 1.22) and the success_bonus (100) is never triggered (mean 0.0). The policy learns to hover/descend slowly using main engine (55% action 2) without completing the landing, because the shaping_reward gives small positive feedback for reducing distance and vertical speed, but the fuel_penalty accumulates over time, making longer episodes worse. The success_bonus is too sparse and the shaping_reward does not provide enough gradient to push the policy to actually land. The leg_contact_bonus (10) is one-shot but only triggers in 20% of episodes. The vertical_speed_penalty is never triggered (mean 0.0) because the policy keeps vertical speed below 0.5. The crash_penalty (-50) is only triggered in the one success-like episode (which also had a crash penalty of -50, likely due to a crash before the success). Overall, the reward structure does not sufficiently incentivize terminal success over timeout.
reflection_diagnosis.component_interaction_diagnosis: fuel_penalty (-0.1 per m_power) dominates the episode-scale reward because the policy uses main engine ~55% of the time over ~954 steps, accumulating ~-52.66. The shaping_reward (+1.22) is positive but small relative to fuel_penalty. The orientation_penalty (-12.47) is the second largest negative component. The success_bonus (100) is never paid, so it provides no gradient. The leg_contact_bonus (10) is one-shot but only paid in 20% of episodes. The vertical_speed_penalty is never triggered because the policy keeps vy < 0.5. The crash_penalty (-50) is only paid in the one success-like episode (which also had a crash). The interaction is: the policy learns to slowly descend using main engine, which reduces distance and vertical speed (positive shaping), but the fuel cost accumulates, making the total reward negative. The policy does not learn to actually land because the success_bonus is too sparse and the shaping_reward does not provide enough incentive to complete the landing. The timeout (0.8 rate) is the terminal outcome, which gives no additional penalty beyond the accumulated fuel_penalty.
reflection_diagnosis.action_coverage_diagnosis: All four discrete actions (0,1,2,3) are used with coverage ratio 1.0. Action 2 (main engine) is dominant at 55.2%, action 0 (do nothing) at 32.8%, action 1 (left orientation) at 7.2%, action 3 (right orientation) at 4.8%. No unused actions. The bottleneck is not action coverage but trajectory-phase completion: the policy does not reliably enter Phase 3 (touchdown). The high main engine usage indicates the policy is trying to descend, but it does not complete the landing.
reflection_diagnosis.failed_pattern_reuse_check: The negative edges from iter_001 to iter_002, iter_003, iter_004, and iter_005 are all closed branches. The common failure pattern across all children was the addition of some form of per-step timeout penalty (ranging from -0.02 to -0.1) combined with other changes (angle relaxation, conditional fuel_penalty, near_pad_bonus, success_bonus increase). The next edit must avoid adding any per-step timeout penalty, must avoid relaxing the success_bonus angle condition, must avoid adding a near_pad_bonus, must avoid increasing the success_bonus scale, and must avoid making the fuel_penalty conditional on altitude. The only change should be reducing the fuel_penalty scale from -0.1 to -0.05, keeping all other components identical to iter_001. This directly addresses the scale imbalance without introducing any of the failed patterns.

edit_summary.target_behavior_plan: The revised reward reduces the fuel_penalty scale from -0.1 to -0.05, halving the dominant penalty. This directly addresses the scale imbalance: the fuel_penalty was 4.22x the next component and 65x the positive objective budget. With the reduced fuel penalty, longer episodes that use main engine for controlled descent will be less costly, allowing the policy to explore landing more aggressively. The success_bonus (100) remains unchanged and provides a strong terminal signal. The shaping_reward (progress-delta) continues to provide positive feedback for reducing distance and vertical speed. The leg_contact_bonus (10) remains one-shot. The crash_penalty (-50) remains unchanged. The orientation_penalty (-0.1) remains unchanged. The vertical_speed_penalty (-1.0) remains unchanged. The expected outcome is that the policy will use main engine more freely near ground, increasing the success_like_terminal_rate from 0.2 to >=0.5 and decreasing timeout_rate from 0.8 to <=0.4.
edit_summary.action_coverage_plan: Action coverage is already 100%. No changes needed. The revised reward should maintain or increase main engine usage for controlled descent and landing.
edit_summary.phase_guidance_plan: Phase 1 (high altitude): shaping_reward encourages descending toward pad, fuel_penalty (now halved) discourages excessive main engine use less strongly. Phase 2 (low altitude): shaping_reward continues, fuel_penalty continues at reduced rate, vertical_speed_penalty discourages hard landings. Phase 3 (touchdown): leg_contact_bonus and success_bonus reward proper landing. The reduced fuel penalty makes all phases less costly, encouraging the policy to explore landing rather than hovering.
edit_summary.payment_mode_plan: success_bonus is sparse (one-shot at terminal success). leg_contact_bonus is event-gated (one-shot). shaping_reward is progress-delta (not repeatable in the same sense). fuel_penalty is dense per-step penalty but now halved. orientation_penalty is dense per-step penalty. vertical_speed_penalty is dense but conditional. crash_penalty is sparse at termination. All positive terms are either sparse, event-gated, or progress-delta. No repeatable positive terms without success.
